output.title: Anonymise first, automate second
output.body:
Before you automate a portfolio workflow, make one decision first: does any document in that flow still contain customer identifiers? If the answer is yes, do not feed the raw sample into AI. Mask or remove names, emails, amounts, contract details, and anything else that would let a person be identified, then test with the cleaned version instead.

That matters most in the ordinary places a small business already works: email, CRM, shared drives, and tools like Zapier or Make. The question is not “can we automate this?” It is “what leaves our control, and where does human review still sit?” If a step already needs a person to check it, keep that checkpoint. If the workflow depends on identifiable data, anonymise a sample before you experiment.

This is not legal advice, and it is not an AI feature. It is a governance rule the owner applies before any build. The clean sample does not remove your obligations, but it does make the next automation decision a lot less messy.
